title: 2021 AMC 12B Problem 18
statement: Let \(z\) be a complex number satisfying \(12|z|^2\) \(=2|z+2|^2+|z^2+1|^2+31.\) What is the value of \(z+\dfrac{6}{z}?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(p=|z|^2=z\bar z\) and \(s=z+\bar z.\) Then \(|z+2|^2=p+2s+4,\) and \(|z^2+1|^2\) \(=p^2+(z^2+\bar z^2)+1\) \(=p^2+(s^2-2p)+1.\)

Substituting, \(12p=2(p+2s+4)\) \(+p^2+s^2-2p+1+31,\) which simplifies to \(p^2-12p+s^2+4s+40=0.\)

Completing the square gives \((p-6)^2+(s+2)^2=0,\) so \(p=6\) and \(s=-2.\)

Then \(z+\dfrac{6}{z}=z+\dfrac{6\bar z}{|z|^2}=z+\bar z=-2.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Let \(p=|z|^2\) and \(s=z+\bar z;\) expand every modulus using \(|w|^2=w\bar w\)
